doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Frank Mitchell
summary: McLean recalls tenor player Frank Mitchell, René's age, who died strangely, from Lee Morgan's Sixth Sense.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh yeah, smiling Billy. Frank Mitchell is another one of them?
I remember him, yeah, but I didn’t have that kind of close association with him.
So that was really just René’s personal friends at that point.
Oh, Frank Mitchell, the tenor player.
Oh yeah. I recorded with him, with Lee, I think.
I think it was – where is it? Somewhere in here, there’s that recording.
Yeah, I remember Frank Mitchell. He died a strange death.
Yeah, very young. It was very – it was René’s age. That’s right. They don’t even have his name in here.
Maybe that’s not the right one, then. But I know you did it on one of Lee’s albums. Here it is. It’s on this one, Sixth Sense.
Yeah, that’s it. He was a young guy that came on the scene, that played very well.
